questions.q: What is the primary reason why independent India needed to repeal or modify many British-era colonial laws?
questions.a: Colonial laws were designed to maintain imperial control, suppress dissent, and extract revenue rather than protect citizens' democratic rights. A wrong answer shows confusion between colonial rule (where subjects had no rights) and constitutional democracy (where citizens hold fundamental rights).

questions.q: Why can't the Parliament simply ignore old colonial laws instead of formally repealing or amending them?
questions.a: Leaving old laws on the books creates legal uncertainty and allows authorities to misuse archaic clauses against citizens exercising their constitutional freedoms. A wrong answer reveals a misunderstanding that laws expire automatically when a country gains independence.

questions.q: Suppose a state police force uses an old colonial-era ordinance to ban a peaceful candle-light march. Which branch of government plays the crucial role in checking whether that old law violates the Constitution?
questions.a: The judiciary plays this crucial role through judicial review, striking down or reading down laws that conflict with Fundamental Rights. A wrong answer indicates the student thinks the police or executive branch decides whether a law is constitutional.

questions.q: Analyze how the doctrine of 'continuity of laws' under Article 373/372 of the Constitution interacted with the need for post-independence legal reform.
questions.a: Article 372 allowed pre-independence laws to continue temporarily so the newly independent nation wouldn't face a legal vacuum, but with the clear mandate that they must gradually be reviewed, amended, or repealed to conform to the new Constitution. A wrong answer shows a belief that either all colonial laws became instantly void in 1950 or that they were permanently approved without changes.

questions.q: Evaluate the argument that keeping certain colonial administrative frameworks ensures state stability, even if some of their original clauses restricted civil liberties.
questions.a: While administrative continuity prevents institutional collapse, maintaining restrictive clauses without reform undermines democratic legitimacy and citizen trust; therefore, courts and lawmakers must systematically purge anti-democratic elements while retaining functional governance procedures. A wrong answer reveals a black-and-white view that either completely destroys state machinery or blindly accepts authoritarian colonial structures.

questions.q: Propose two specific criteria a law commission should use to decide whether a pre-independence law should be permanently repealed today.
questions.a: Criteria should include: 1) Does the law conflict with any current Fundamental Right? 2) Is the objective of the law maintaining colonial dominance rather than public welfare or safety? A poor answer suggests repealing laws purely based on how old they are without analyzing their democratic function.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Repealing colonial laws refers to the post-independence legislative and judicial process of formally revoking or replacing outdated statutes enacted by the British colonial ______ that violated fundamental rights or sovereignty, ensuring that all laws governing independent India align with the democratic values of the Indian Constitution.
Fill in the blank: Imagine ______ a rulebook from an old school that punished students just for questioning the headmaster, even if the question was fair.
What is Repealing colonial laws? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Repealing colonial laws refers to the post-independence legislative and judicial process of formally revoking or replacing outdated statutes enacted by the British colonial administration that violated fundamental rights or sovereignty, ensuring that all laws governing independent India align with the democratic values of the Indian.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: When India became a republic in ______, it inherited hundreds of laws written by the British Raj to control citizens rather than serve them.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Repealing colonial laws?
questions.a: Students often think that once India adopted its Constitution in 1950, all British-era laws automatically disappeared overnight.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Students can explain why colonial laws needed removal after independence, distinguish between laws that served imperial control versus those serving citizen welfare, and identify how the judiciary and legislature work together to review and repeal archaic legislation.
